questions.q: The editorial recalls a simple comparison about tension: “When it rains, you don’t demand that it stop raining…” How does it end?
options: “…rather you stay indoors until it ends”
Not quite. The article says: “…rather you use an umbrella” – find a way to manage stress instead of becoming anxious.
“…rather you move to a drier place”
Not quite. The article says: “…rather you use an umbrella” – find a way to manage stress instead of becoming anxious.
“…rather you complain to the authorities”
Not quite. The article says: “…rather you use an umbrella” – find a way to manage stress instead of becoming anxious.
“…rather you use an umbrella” – find a way to manage stress instead of becoming anxious
Yes. Tension is as natural as rain.
questions.rationale: “When it rains, you don’t demand that it stop raining, rather you use an umbrella. When faced with stress, find a solution to it instead of becoming anxious.”

questions.q: Modern comforts have made many old dreams real, yet joy still eludes people. What reason does the article give?
options: Happiness was easier in the past
Not quite. The article says: They try to understand life from its short pre-death phase alone, leaving out the eternal phase after death.
People work too little
Not quite. The article says: They try to understand life from its short pre-death phase alone, leaving out the eternal phase after death.
Comforts are still too few
Not quite. The article says: They try to understand life from its short pre-death phase alone, leaving out the eternal phase after death.
They try to understand life from its short pre-death phase alone, leaving out the eternal phase after death
Well reasoned. The whole gives the part its meaning.
questions.rationale: “There is only one reason for this tragic state of affairs. And that is, trying to understand life keeping only the pre-death period of life in mind.”

questions.q: With what image does the article describe the two phases of human life?
options: This life is a road; the next is a bridge
Not quite. The article says: This life is for sowing the seed; the life after death is for gathering the harvest.
This life is a dream; the next is sleep
Not quite. The article says: This life is for sowing the seed; the life after death is for gathering the harvest.
This life is a lamp; the next is its shadow
Not quite. The article says: This life is for sowing the seed; the life after death is for gathering the harvest.
This life is for sowing the seed; the life after death is for gathering the harvest
Right. No fruit without sowing.
questions.rationale: “The pre-death period of man’s life is the period for sowing seeds, as it were. The post-death period of man’s life is the period for harvesting the fruit.”

questions.q: How did Aisha describe the Prophet’s way of speaking?
options: Rapidly, to cover many subjects
Not quite. The article says: Slowly and clearly, pausing between sentences, so that one could have counted his words.
Slowly and clearly, pausing between sentences, so that one could have counted his words
Yes. Never loud or coarse.
Very rarely, and then at great length
Not quite. The article says: Slowly and clearly, pausing between sentences, so that one could have counted his words.
In verse, to delight his hearers
Not quite. The article says: Slowly and clearly, pausing between sentences, so that one could have counted his words.
questions.rationale: “The Prophet would not speak fast as you people do. He used to pause in between sentences, giving people time to memorize what he had said.”

questions.q: Why, according to the article, does a believer weigh his words before speaking?
options: He is afraid of being laughed at
Not quite. The article says: He knows every word is recorded and that he must answer to God for it.
He knows every word is recorded and that he must answer to God for it
Correct. Fear of God restrains idle talk.
He wishes to appear wise
Not quite. The article says: He knows every word is recorded and that he must answer to God for it.
He has little to say
Not quite. The article says: He knows every word is recorded and that he must answer to God for it.
questions.rationale: “Aware of the fact that he will have to answer to God for everything he says, he assumes a deep sense of responsibility.”

questions.q: A young woman, miserable in a desert village, wrote that she was coming home. What two lines did her father send in reply?
options: “Home is where the heart is; come when you wish”
Not quite. The article says: “Two men looked out from prison bars, one saw mud, and the other saw stars”.
“The darkest hour is before the dawn”
Not quite. The article says: “Two men looked out from prison bars, one saw mud, and the other saw stars”.
“Two men looked out from prison bars, one saw mud, and the other saw stars”
Right. She resolved to look for the stars.
“A rolling stone gathers no moss”
Not quite. The article says: “Two men looked out from prison bars, one saw mud, and the other saw stars”.
questions.rationale: “Two men looked out from prison bars, one saw mud, and the other saw stars.”

questions.q: She came to love the desert and wrote a successful book about it. What, according to the article, had actually changed?
options: The villagers had learned her language
Not quite. The article says: Only her own attitude – nothing in her surroundings.
The climate had become milder
Not quite. The article says: Only her own attitude – nothing in her surroundings.
Her husband had been posted elsewhere
Not quite. The article says: Only her own attitude – nothing in her surroundings.
Only her own attitude – nothing in her surroundings
Well read. A change within gave her a new life.
questions.rationale: “Neither the desert, nor the natives, nor any other element in the situation had changed. Whatever change had taken place was inside the mind and heart of Thelma Thompson.”

questions.q: Botanists say as much of a tree lies below ground as above. What lesson does the article draw?
options: What is seen matters most
Not quite. The article says: To grow outwardly one must first build strength inwardly – begin with oneself before rebuilding society.
The hidden half is wasted
Not quite. The article says: To grow outwardly one must first build strength inwardly – begin with oneself before rebuilding society.
Trees should be planted deeper
Not quite. The article says: To grow outwardly one must first build strength inwardly – begin with oneself before rebuilding society.
To grow outwardly one must first build strength inwardly – begin with oneself before rebuilding society
Yes. “Root downward, fruit upward.”
questions.rationale: “If we seek to progress outwardly, we must first strengthen ourselves inwardly. We must begin from the base of our own selves before we can hope to build society anew.”

questions.q: What does a mountain stream do when stones block its path, and what does this teach?
options: It wears the stones away by force
Not quite. The article says: It flows around them – do not collide with obstacles, but find a way past and keep going.
It flows around them – do not collide with obstacles, but find a way past and keep going
Exactly. Avoidance, not confrontation.
It stops until the stones are removed
Not quite. The article says: It flows around them – do not collide with obstacles, but find a way past and keep going.
It turns back to its source
Not quite. The article says: It flows around them – do not collide with obstacles, but find a way past and keep going.
questions.rationale: “The spring does not attempt to remove the stones to continue its journey. Instead, it carves its way ahead around and alongside the stones.”

questions.q: Sun, air and plants all give without taking in return. How is man’s following of this model meant to differ from nature’s?
options: Nature follows it by compulsion; man is to adopt it consciously, of his own free will
Well reasoned. Living as a giver by choice.
Man may take twice what he gives
Not quite. The article says: Nature follows it by compulsion; man is to adopt it consciously, of his own free will.
Man is exempt from it
Not quite. The article says: Nature follows it by compulsion; man is to adopt it consciously, of his own free will.
Man need follow it only in youth
Not quite. The article says: Nature follows it by compulsion; man is to adopt it consciously, of his own free will.
questions.rationale: “In the rest of the universe, the model has been established compulsively, under the laws of nature, while we have to adopt this model in our lives consciously, of our own free will.”
